profile.org_note: Partner-run private builder: three managing partners (Saun Sullivan, CEO; Jeff Purpera Jr., CFO; Lee Foster, COO) make the land and finance decisions, and local land records show Purpera personally signing lot purchases. The site lists seven operating areas with their own offices (Louisiana, North Alabama, South Alabama, Florida, Mississippi, Tennessee, Texas) under affiliated entities DSLD Homes, LLC; DSLD Homes (Gulf Coast), LLC; DSLD Homes (Florida), LLC; DSLD Homes (Southwest), LLC; and DSLD Homes (Southeast), LLC, but names no area or division leader. Purpera and Foster are also the listed directors of Pavo Capital Inc., a Baton Rouge lot-holding company active in 2025.
profile.email_pattern: first initial + last name @dsldhomes.com (for example tsandifer@dsldhomes.com for Tyler Sandifer)
profile.summary: Largest private homebuilder in the Gulf South: 120+ active communities across Louisiana, southern Mississippi, Alabama, Tennessee, Texas and Northwest Florida, and homes built for 41,000+ families, selling entry-level 'affordable quality' homes. Baton Rouge Business Report put it in the local $1 billion revenue club in Nov 2025, with 550+ staff, 20-plus offices and Louisiana down to about 65% of closings from 95%. It mostly buys finished lots in phases from local developers (repeated recorded takedowns in 2024 to 2026), and the partners run a related lot-holding company, so a land banker's counterparty is the three-partner group, above all the CFO.

people.name: Jeff Purpera Jr.
people.title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO); partner
people.prior_role: Worked under founder Allen Thomason with Sullivan and Foster before the three took over management (The Advocate, 2020; Business Report, 2018).
people.source_title: Baton Rouge Business Report: The road to $1 billion (photo caption: Jeff Purpera, CFO, DSLD Homes)
people.note: Also printed as Jeffery Purpera / Jeffery Purpera Jr. First call for a land banker: he is both the finance head and the person who signs lot purchases. Business Report land-record items name him as DSLD's signatory on lot takedowns (Zachary, Nov 2024; Reserve at Conway, Jan 2025) and call him 'one of DSLD's partners' who represented both buyer and seller when DSLD bought 71 and 83 lots from Livingston Parc LLC (Apr and Nov 2025: https://www.businessreport.com/dsld-acquires-83-more-lots-in-denham-springs-development/). In the Nov 2025 caption he refers to 'bankers and bondholders' asking how big DSLD plans to get, which implies bank lines and some form of bond debt. Business filings cited by Business Report list him and Lee Foster as directors of Pavo Capital Inc., a Baton Rouge lot-holding company (https://www.businessreport.com/this-company-just-bought-over-30-lots-in-the-highlandia-community/, Apr 2025). CFO since at least April 2014 (Business Report). No treasurer or separate capital-markets officer is published, so he appears to cover those functions. Email is built from the company pattern and is not confirmed.

people.name: Lee Foster
people.title: Chief Operating Officer; partner
people.prior_role: Described in 2020 as manager of construction and building; came up under founder Allen Thomason (The Advocate, 2020).
people.source_title: Baton Rouge Business Report: Could a moratorium in Livingston deter future development there? (names Lee Foster, chief operating officer)
people.note: Tagged Inferred only because the COO title was last published in Aug 2023; the person is confirmed active in 2025. Business Report land-record items from Apr to Jul 2025 show him signing lot purchases for Pavo Capital Inc. (33 lots in Highlandia, 31 in Atwater Reserve, 23 in Water's Edge, 70 in Delaune Estates for $6.7M: https://www.businessreport.com/local-holding-company-acquires-70-lots-in-ascension-development/), and business filings cited there list him and Jeff Purpera as Pavo's directors. In the Highlandia case the seller said Pavo planned to resell the lots to other local builders, so Pavo looks like the partners' own lot-holding vehicle. One of the three DSLD partners (Business Report, 2018). Listed on the Home Builders Association of Greater Baton Rouge board for DSLD Homes in 2024 (The Advocate, 2024-01-07). Email is built from the company pattern and is not confirmed.

people.note: Senior of the three managing partners (Sullivan, Purpera, Foster) who took over from the founder. The company site names no other executive. Email is built from the company pattern and is not confirmed.

people.note: Role is inferred from land records, not from a published title: Business Report says he represented DSLD when it bought 51 Atwater Villas lots for $3.8M (Sep 2025) and 91 Dogwood Trace lots in Walker (Dec 2024: https://www.businessreport.com/this-livingston-parish-community-is-about-to-get-90-plus-new-homes/). A 'D. Brian Cohn' also signed for West Village Development CDL LLC, described as a Covington company, on a 43-acre Baton Rouge tract in Sep 2025. Whether he is a DSLD employee, an affiliated developer or counsel is not public. Confirm before calling. Title note: Signs lot purchases for DSLD.

gaps: Head of land acquisition / land development: no title published anywhere found. Lot purchases are signed by CFO-partner Jeff Purpera Jr. and by Brian Cohn (title not public).
Treasurer / capital markets: not publicly disclosed; no role separate from the CFO was found.
President: no one publicly carries the title; CEO Saun Sullivan and COO Lee Foster are the published operating leads.

Regional and division leaders (Louisiana sub-markets, North Alabama/Huntsville, South Alabama, Florida Panhandle, Mississippi Gulf Coast, Tennessee, Texas): not named on the company site, which lists only offices and sales representatives; none found in the press reached in this run.
Lee Foster's COO title was last published in Aug 2023; 2025 sources confirm he is active but do not restate the title.
Brian Cohn and Chris Clare: DSLD job titles not published.

Headquarters: the company site, Business Report (Nov 2025) and the Alabama Secretary of State record all give 7660 Pecue Lane, Baton Rouge; the ranking and older press say Denham Springs, where the company started (1220 S. Range Avenue).
Ownership split among the partners and any outside investor: not publicly disclosed.
Direct phone numbers and confirmed emails for the partners: not published; emails shown are pattern-built.

Search coverage was limited: the shared web-search allowance was exhausted before this run, so people were found through the company site, Business Report's and The Advocate's own site search, HBA board pages and the Alabama corporate registry. Trade press (Builder, Pro Builder), local outlets outside Baton Rouge, the Louisiana, Florida, Tennessee and Texas corporate registries, and most Business Report article bodies (paywalled) were not reviewed. Division leaders may be findable with a fresh search allowance.
